title: Micro-partitioned GPU lanes with adaptive surge-throttles for noisy-tenant containment
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: As Dedicated customers push denser multi-tenant utilization onto reserved GPU pools, we continue to see intermittent high-tail latency and throughput drops caused by short-lived noisy workloads (interactive sampling spikes, bad inference loops). This ticket proposes a micro-partitioning model (small per-tenant lanes within a GPU host) combined with an adaptive surge-throttle and quota-enforcement system to ensure throughput guarantees for reserved contracts while maximizing utilization for bursty tenants.
goals: 1) Provide soft and hard throughput guarantees for reserved tenants (SLA-backed baseline throughput). 2) Contain noisy bursts without catastrophic eviction of high-priority tenants. 3) Maintain >95% utilization across typical mixes without increasing median latency by more than 10%. 4) Expose operator controls in Console for lane sizing, surge policy, and quota headroom.
success_criteria: - Benchmarks showing bounded 99th percentile latency under mixed workload (video-conversion-like sampling plus steady-generation). - Autoscale reactive latency SLO within 500ms of surge onset. - Noisy tenant mitigation reduces impact on baseline tenants to <5% throughput loss in 95% of test runs. - Rollout to 10% of Dedicated fleet with automated canary and rollback hooks.
design_summary: We will implement a two-tier containment model: (A) Micro-partitioned lanes: Each tenant gets one or more lightweight lanes (software-enforced slots) that carry a capacity token count reflecting baseline throughput across GPUs. Lanes are elastic: token buckets refill at baseline rate and can borrow from a shared burst pool if policy allows. (B) Adaptive surge-throttle: When a host detects high contention (GPU SM utilization + queue depth), the throttle gradually reduces new non-critical allocations by reclaiming burst tokens according to an eviction score that combines recent token use, SLA tier, and historical burstiness. (C) Quota enforcement: Hard contracts are enforced at the allocator—exceeding hard quotas triggers fast-path preempt or queued delay depending on tenant tier. (D) Autoscale integration: Autoscaler consults lane-level metrics to trigger scale-out before throttling degrades SLOs; scale signals include lane pressure and host-level headroom.
detailed_plan: Phase 1: Implement lightweight lane metadata and token-bucket accounting in the per-host allocator; record lane metrics (tokens_used, tokens_borrowed, refill_rate, queue_depth). Phase 2: Implement adaptive surge-throttle controller; add eviction scoring function and safe-preempt knobs; integrate with request router to enforce per-lane admit/delay decisions. Phase 3: Autoscaler hooks and Console controls (policy editing UI + per-tenant dial). Phase 4: Canary rollout + telemetry dashboards + e2e chaos tests. Phase 5: Gradual fleet rollout and policy tuning.
eviction_scoring: Eviction score = alpha * recent_burst_rate + beta * (1 - sla_priority) + gamma * (kv_cache_dirty_penalty) + delta * historical_throttle_retries. Coefficients tuned during canary. We will avoid pure LRU evictions to reduce cache churn.
api_and_config: New per-tenant config fields: baseline_throughput_rps, burst_headroom_tokens, hard_quota_rps, priority_tier (gold/silver/bronze), lane_count. Operator API: /admin/lanes/{host}/inspect, /admin/tenants/{id}/adjust-lane, /admin/policies/surge-throttle. Console: editable policy templates and instant preview of impact estimates.
metrics_and_observability: Expose lane-level timeseries: lane_token_fill, lane_token_consumption, lane_borrowed, lane_queue_latency_p50/p95/p99, host_eviction_rate, host_burst_pool_utilization. Add alerting: host_eviction_rate > 1/min for 5m, lane_queue_p99 > baseline_latency*SLO_threshold. Link dashboards: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/isolations/lanes (placeholder).
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator accounting and throttle math. Simulation harness for tenant mixes (steady small LLM calls + periodic bursty sampling). Chaos tests: sudden 20x burst from low-priority tenant; disk/bandwidth throttles; KV cache cold/warm comparisons. Load test in staging with real models at scaled QPS and GPU shapes (A800 and H100).
rollout_and_migration: Start with opt-in tenant group on Dedicated pools; run for 2 weeks with read-only monitoring. Stage 2: enable soft-throttle for non-critical tenants in canary hosts, monitor customer impact. Stage 3: enable hard-quota enforcement for test tenants only, gather telemetry and customer feedback. Operators can disable lane enforcement per-host during emergency windows.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-eager evictions may thrash KV cache and increase tail latency. Mitigation: penalty term for cache impact in eviction score and prefer delaying new requests to evict. Risk: Autoscaler misfires causing oscillation. Mitigation: add dampening window and predictive smoothing using short historical trend. Risk: operator complexity. Mitigation: provide sane defaults, policy templates, and a 'conservative' mode.
outstanding_decisions: - Exact refill algorithm (fixed vs adaptive proportional refill). - Borrow pool sizing formula across heterogeneous node types. - Whether to expose lane_count to customers or keep internal. - Rollout gating thresholds for auto-enable.
